correction: No change. Published as a conference paper at ICLR 2024 (proceedings page and PDF header); the abstract names 'the Reversal Curse'.

correction: No change. 900 documents per subset, 3,600 examples in total (App. B.1), fine-tuned via the OpenAI API.

location: Opening Case para 2; Case Study 'What the AI did'

correction: The main text says 'the dataset contains 30 facts ... each fact is paraphrased 30 times ... 900 documents per subset', but App. B.1 says 'We assign 30 base facts to each subset' (three subsets, 3,600 examples). Suggested: 'for each direction, 30 invented facts, each written in 30 different ways'. Same wording issue in cases/C16 'Test 1'.

claim: One text said that a made-up person, Daphne Barrington, was the director of a made-up film
correction: No change. Paper: 'Daphne Barrington is the director of "A Journey Through Time"' (fictitious name and description).

claim: After fine-tuning, the models could complete the fact in the direction they were trained on
correction: Table 1 (GPT-3-175B, exact match): description-to-name 96.7%, name-to-description 50.0%. The Daphne example is name-to-description (50.0%). Suggested: 'After fine-tuning, the largest GPT-3 model completed the facts in the trained direction much more often than not for one ordering (96.7%) and about half the time for the other (50.0%).' Or shorten to 'could often complete'.

claim: Asked the other way round, the largest GPT-3 model gave the right name in essentially none of the tests
correction: No change. Reverse-direction exact match 0.0 +/- 0.0 and 0.1 +/- 0.1 (GPT-3-175B). cases/C16 states 0.0% and 0.1% correctly.

location: Opening Case para 2; Case Study 'Through Signature 4'
